record.original_question: Find a decoding algorithm for quadratic residue codes, since the chapter states that no decoding algorithm was known for them.

evidence.quote: There is no decoding algorithm known for QR codes.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $p$ be an odd prime such that $2$ is a quadratic residue modulo $p$, and let $\mathbb{F}_2$ denote the binary field. Let $Q \subset \mathbb{F}_p^{\times}$ be the set of nonzero quadratic residues modulo $p$, and let $\alpha$ be a primitive $p$-th root of unity in some extension field of $\mathbb{F}_2$. The (binary) quadratic residue code of length $p$ is the cyclic code $\mathcal{Q} \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^p$ whose generator polynomial is
$$g(x) = \prod_{i \in Q} (x - \alpha^i) \in \mathbb{F}_2[x].$$
Such codes have minimum distance $d$ satisfying $d^2 \geq p$ (the square-root bound) and the designed error-correcting capability $t = \lfloor (d-1)/2 \rfloor$.

Problem: Construct an explicit decoding algorithm that, given any received word $r = c + e \in \mathbb{F}_2^p$ where $c \in \mathcal{Q}$ and $e$ has Hamming weight at most $t$, recovers the error vector $e$ (and hence the codeword $c$). The algorithm should work for general primes $p$ in the above family, achieving the full error-correcting capability of the code up to half the minimum distance.
artifact.status_search_result: Since the late 1980s, many algebraic decoding algorithms have been developed for binary quadratic residue (QR) codes, including methods based on the Berlekamp–Massey algorithm, lookup tables, syndrome-weight decoding, and difference-of-syndromes techniques. These algorithms successfully decode binary QR codes up to half the minimum distance for code lengths up to roughly 113 (with explicit algorithms published for lengths 41, 47, 71, 73, 79, 89, 97, 113). However, decoding long binary QR codes and non-binary QR codes in full generality remains an active research problem.

status_evidence.snippet: Algebraic decoding algorithm for the (89,45,17) binary QR code.
status_evidence.claim: Explicit algebraic decoding algorithms exist for specific QR codes.

status_evidence.title: An Improved Decoding Algorithm to Decode Quadratic Residue Codes Based on the Difference of Syndromes
status_evidence.snippet: An improved difference-of-syndromes decoding algorithm for QR codes up to half the minimum distance.
status_evidence.claim: Recent algorithms decode QR codes up to their error-correcting capability.

status_evidence.title: Quadratic residue code - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Quadratic residue codes are a family of cyclic codes; decoding algorithms have been developed for many specific lengths.
status_evidence.claim: Multiple decoding algorithms now exist; general decoding for long QR codes remains open.
